welcome.lead: Send an AI one text and everything is fine. Send it a thousand, and problems appear that no demo shows. Kuyruk is an AI service built to find those problems, measure them, and fix each one with the smallest possible change.
welcome.p1_title: One slow AI call freezes the service for everyone.
welcome.p1_note: The code looks perfectly normal. But while the AI thinks, nobody else gets an answer, not even a simple "are you alive?".
welcome.p1_fix: Wait for the AI the right way, so the service keeps helping others in the meantime. One word in the code.
welcome.p1_result: The time to answer "are you alive?" while {e1_slow_requests} slow jobs run.
welcome.p2_title: Restart the server mid-job, and the job vanishes.
welcome.p2_note: It still says "running". Forever. Servers restart all the time, with every update, and nobody is told the work is gone.
welcome.p2_fix: Save every result the moment it's ready, and let a separate worker send a heartbeat. When the heartbeat goes quiet, another worker takes over.
welcome.p2_result: Killed halfway through, the job carried on about {e2_recovery_about_s} seconds later and finished every text.
welcome.p3_title: Every update ships a {e3_bad_gb} GB package.
welcome.p3_note: Slow to send, slow to start, and every small change rebuilds everything from scratch.
welcome.p3_fix: Start from a slim base, and build in the right order so unchanged steps are reused. The surprise: one line did {e3_base_percent}% of the work.
welcome.p3_result: {e3_bad_mb} MB down to {e3_good_mb} MB, and rebuilds after a code change {e3_times_faster} times faster.
welcome.p4_title: Everyone says: add a cache to speed up your checks.
welcome.p4_note: It's in every guide. So teams add it, and never check whether it helps.
welcome.p4_fix: Measure before you optimise. {e4_runs} runs, half with the cache and half without, on the same code.
welcome.p4_result: {e4_cache_on_s} seconds with the cache, {e4_cache_off_s} without. Good advice in general isn't always good advice for you.
welcome.how_lead: Every fix above is built into Kuyruk. Use it on your own Turkish texts.
welcome.s1_text: Up to {max_texts} texts. Clean them, count their cost, or summarise each in one sentence.
welcome.s2_text: You get a ticket at once. The work carries on without you, even through a crash.
welcome.s3_text: Every result next to its original, ready to download.
welcome.cta_title: Don't take our word for it.
welcome.cta_text: Start a job, then crash the worker yourself. Watch Kuyruk notice, and finish anyway.
welcome.footer: The stack is standard; the experiments and decisions are mine. Adar Palaoğlu

experiments.lead: Each experiment breaks a standard AI service in a way that happens in real life, measures the damage, then tests the smallest fix. Every prediction was written down before the first measurement.
experiments.e1_title: One person's slow job froze the service for everyone.
experiments.e1_never: with one user, the code works perfectly. The freeze only appears when many slow requests arrive at once.
experiments.e1_did: Sent {e1_slow_requests} slow requests, and asked "are you alive?" every tenth of a second. Wrote the same step three ways.
experiments.e1_fix: Wait for the AI in a way that lets the service keep working. And make the health check itself never wait in line.
experiments.e1_bad_caption: to answer, written the usual way
experiments.e2_title: A restart in the middle of a job lost all the work that was left.
experiments.e2_never: the job still says "running", and the health check still says everything is fine. There's no error. It just never finishes.
experiments.e2_did: Killed the program halfway through a job, with no warning, like a power cut. {e2_broken_runs} times without the fix, {e2_fixed_runs} times with it, including {e2_ai_runs} with the real AI.
experiments.e2_fix: A separate worker with a heartbeat. When it goes quiet for {e2_stale_s} seconds, another worker carries on from the first unfinished text.
experiments.e2_good_caption: with the fix · back in {e2_recovery_min_s}–{e2_recovery_max_s} s
experiments.e3_title: Every update shipped a {e3_bad_gb} GB package.
experiments.e3_never: it still works. It's just slow to send, slow to start, and every one-line change rebuilds everything.
experiments.e3_did: Built five versions that each change one thing, {e3_builds} builds on two different machines.
experiments.e3_surprise: One line, the starting image, did {e3_base_percent}% of the work. The fancy tricks added {e3_rest_percent}%. Build order is what makes rebuilds fast.
experiments.e4_title: The speed-up everyone recommends did nothing.
experiments.e4_never: nobody measures a cache after adding it. It's in every guide, so it must help.
experiments.e4_did: Ran the checks {e4_runs} times on GitHub, half with the cache and half without, on the same code.
experiments.e4_lesson: Downloading took under half a second, so there was nothing to save. Measure before you optimise. And the publishing step, which holds the secret, ran only for real updates: skipped in all {e4_release_skipped} test runs.
experiments.cost_title: Turkish costs more to send to an AI.
experiments.cost_note: more tokens for the same {cost_reviews} reviews. Turkish uses fewer words, but each word is cut into almost twice as many pieces: {cost_tr_per_word} against {cost_en_per_word}.
experiments.crash_title: Don't take our word for it.
